primary_claim: Stratified Inoculation Prompting (SIP), which assigns diverse non-eliciting control prompts to confidently safe (desired-trait-only) training examples instead of the uniform inoculation prompt, substantially reduces undesired-trait leakage to non-eliciting prompts (down to the level of a full desired-trait-only SFT reference) while better preserving the desired trait than standard uniform Inoculation Prompting, needs as little as 5% distinct safe data (oversampled to 25% of training positions), and yields lower Emergent Misalignment point estimates than uniform IP in two harmful-advice settings.

effect.value: SIP reduces leakage to the level of the DT-only SFT reference (vs substantial leakage under Uniform IP); good performance achieved with only 5% distinct DT-only data oversampled to 25% of positions; SIP yields lower Emergent Misalignment point estimates than Uniform IP in both harmful-advice settings

contradicts_or_qualifies: Addresses the underspecification problem in standard Inoculation Prompting (Tan et al. 2025; Wichers et al. 2025), which pairs every example with the same inoculation prompt and leaves the activation boundary underspecified, producing backdoor leakage (Dubinski et al. 2026) and suppressed desired-trait generalization related to the conditionalisation confound

Notes the Inoculation Adapters approach tackles the same underspecification structurally via a frozen LoRA rather than prompt conditioning; SIP instead retains prompt conditioning but adds contrastive training evidence
limitations_stated: Studies five controlled two-trait settings across three instruction-tuned model families from 7B to 24B; real data contamination may involve several interacting or hard-to-elicit/judge traits not cleanly separable
Partition-error experiments use synthetic, controlled classification errors, which may differ from the more structured errors of real classifiers
SIP is tested only during supervised fine-tuning, not whether the learned conditional boundary survives subsequent outcome-based RL or other post-training
SIP narrows the backdoor's activation boundary rather than removing the undesired trait; the exact inoculation prompt remains a reliable trigger unless combined with dilution or password-locking
quote: Compared to standard IP, SIP significantly reduces leakage and retains more of the desired trait.
